reason: The vulnerable daemon authorization package is not linked into this client tool. Revalidated against nonempty Go package symbol evidence for every scanned binary. Missing, ambiguous or affected symbol evidence must fail closed on both rebuilt and published images.

verified_debian_applicability.reason: CVE-2026-24882 affects PKDECRYPT handling in tpm2d/command.c, built into the separately packaged tpm2daemon, not the agent IPC stub. Both complete hosted inventories omit that daemon and its package. Bind every installed GnuPG companion version and the authenticated Debian native payloads; invalidate this review when the daemon reappears or evidence expires.

The vulnerable analyze_string implementation occurs in progs/infocmp.c, not the shipped ncurses libraries. Require the exact native libraries and complete inventory proving infocmp and ncurses-bin absent. No other ncurses advisory is covered.

add_to_challenge is in plugins/digestmd5.c and the separately packaged DIGEST-MD5 plugin. The image contains the core SASL library and DB plugin only. Bind their exact official native bytes and require the affected plugin/package to remain absent from a complete inventory.

The advisory concerns Python SAX attributeDecl reference handling in python/libxml.c. That Python extension is not part of the native libxml2 shared library and is absent from the image. Require the native library hash plus absence of binding files and packages; all other libxml2 advisories remain blocking.

CERT-PL's CNA record restricts CVE-2026-40469 to 32-bit builds. The authenticated native Debian executables matching the hosted images are ELFCLASS64 with EM_X86_64 and EM_AARCH64 respectively. Bind those executable bytes and architecture-specific binNMU versions; no other gawk advisory is excluded.

The CNA affected range starts at 1.3.1.2. The exact Debian upstream source is 1.3.1, contains no gz_vacate implementation, and its packaging has an empty patch series. Native library bytes were compared to authenticated Debian packages and both hosted SBOMs. This does not cover any later package or another zlib advisory.

Upstream's CVE-2026-95619 fix states the POSIX implementation is unaffected. All shipped native, i386 and x32 configurations define _GLIBCXX_HAVE_POSIX_MEMALIGN=1. The aligned-new shared-library routines call posix_memalign and each libstdc++/libsupc++ new_opa.o archive member references it, bypassing the affected rounding branches. Require every inspected shared/static payload and config header plus the exact GCC source-package family. CVE-2026-102010 remains blocking.

verified_debian_backports.reason: Official Trixie backports packages contain curl 8.21.0. For these eight advisories only, curl's upstream OSV records explicitly mark 8.21.0 fixed and exclude it from affected versions; Debian's sid fixed versions agree, while the unbounded Trixie source-package records remain open. On both architectures, the executable and both TLS libraries in run 42018140474 match packages downloaded through authenticated Debian APT indexes. The transitional GnuTLS package must also match. The other 23 curl advisories remain blocking; this is verified remediation, not risk acceptance.

Built from stable util-linux 2.41.6 with Trixie packaging: upstream fixes failed-helper hooks and restricted source resolution. The local patch completes nsenter descriptor closure, includes fileutils.h in the idmap hook and corrects RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS to Linux UAPI 0x04 (patch SHA-256 ec260c3fe82a0385a1ce7afe2c1c592d57729f134a22f1447af5ec28c69e529d). CVE-2026-78409 is not reviewed: absence of the 2.42 fast path alone does not settle older open_tree paths. Package tests and direct final/intermediate symlink rejection checks pass; kernel-denied inotify/personality prerequisites are explicitly reported as skipped. Match every native payload below before reviewing these three source-package advisories.

The pinned upstream patch corrects the filename boundary; the local patch bounds the Metalink reverse scan and checks HTML quote allocation arithmetic. The source builder runs the package tests and ASan/UBSan bounds regressions. Native executable hashes are verified against the same-run archives from 41892997468 at 08522d32554d34f88a40351f8c110ff9a1d0a5f6. Only these three patched advisories are reviewed.

Replace the vulnerable core modules in place with checksum-pinned Archive::Tar 3.14 and podlators 6.1.1. Their upstream tests pass. Require all reviewed module files, not a vendor copy shadowing unchanged core code.

These two Perl source-package advisories affect bundled pure-Perl modules, not interpreter C code. The unchanged native packages are reviewed only when every affected core module file matches the in-place Archive::Tar 3.14/podlators 6.1.1 replacement. No other Perl advisory is covered.

The reviewed ncurses source contains the fix. Both native libraries and exact package versions must match.

The pinned GnuPG source includes the fix. Match all native executables and exact companion package versions; signing, verification and tampered-message rejection pass in the assembled runtime.

GNU gawk 5.4.1 includes the four upstream fixes documented in its ChangeLog. The release signature was verified using the GNU keyring (D1967C63788713177D861ED7DF597815937EC0D2). Require exact native executable bytes; the enabled upstream tests pass non-root. PMA is disabled for sandbox compatibility, not as an advisory exclusion.

The checksum-pinned Debian libxml2 2.15.4 source contains the upstream fixes. Match the exact local package and native shared library before reviewing the unbounded Trixie source-package findings. The Perl consumer is rebuilt for the new ABI and its 2577 tests pass on AMD64; the old library is absent from the runtime.

The checksum-pinned Python 3.13.18 Debian source includes these fixes. Match the exact interpreter (including built-in XML modules), SSL extension, corrected Python modules and Expat 2.10 payload before reviewing Trixie's unbounded findings. Missing-hostname rejection is regression-tested; other packages and advisories remain blocking.

The checksum-pinned Debian curl 8.23.0-1 source includes these upstream fixes. Trixie's unbounded open advisory records also match this local backport. Apply only when all four exact package versions and all three native payload SHA-256 values match the reviewed build; otherwise retain the findings.
